acceptance: A short decision note in the PR body compares A and B with measured extra runner-minutes per day from the last 7 days of trunk runs

For the chosen approach: a test or workflow assertion shows that a superseded develop push still produces dist-<sha>-attempt-N (A), or that admit and trunk UAT select the newest dist-bearing commit with a clear error otherwise (B)
Live check after merge: two develop merges within 5 minutes both end with a dist artifact (A), or the documented selection works on a real run (B)
No change to what the dist contains or how it is built (the wheel and sdist digests for the same commit are unchanged)
context: Member of batch release-v2-remediation (see rv2r-01 context). GUARDRAILS: do not change dist build steps or artifact names; keep cancel-in-progress semantics for the test jobs. DECISION GATE: if extra cost exceeds 60 runner-minutes per day, stop and ask the owner before choosing A.
description: Since 2026-10-28, 42 of 100 trunk runs were cancelled when a newer push replaced them. A commit without a trunk dist artifact cannot be released (docs/internal/release-artifacts.md:8-11), and continuous trunk UAT also needs that dist. Choose and implement one approach: (A) build and upload the dist in a separate trunk job that is never cancelled (for example its own concurrency group), or (B) make the release and trunk UAT always use the newest commit that has a dist, and document that rule. Measure runner cost before choosing.
